title: Distinct Arrangements
statement:
You have a row of tiles, each showing a lowercase letter (`text`); some letters may repeat. You can arrange the tiles in a row in many ways, but two arrangements that look the same count only once (swapping two identical letters changes nothing).

Return the **number of different arrangements** of all the tiles.
constraints: text contains only lowercase letters a-z

hints.nudge: If all letters were different there would be n! arrangements. What happens to that number when a letter appears twice?
hints.pattern: Count with a formula: divide by the number of ways to reorder identical letters. (Or recurse on 'which letter goes first', using letter counts.)
hints.pseudocode:
answer = n!
for each letter that appears c times: answer = answer / c!
return answer
hints.walkthrough: Listing every arrangement and removing duplicates works for tiny inputs but explodes quickly (12 letters give up to 479 million arrangements). Counting is easier: n! orders if all tiles were different, but each group of c identical tiles can be reordered among themselves in c! ways without changing the arrangement, so divide by c! for every letter. The recursive view gives the same count: choose the first letter among the distinct letters left, then count the arrangements of the rest. For n <= 12 every number involved fits in a 32-bit int (12! = 479001600).
